## Background

Portfolio piece — a synthetic recreation of a dose-response analysis I
helped run during a colleague's MSc project. The pipeline takes a
plate-level "% of control" response across a range of doses and three
stressors — **NaCl** (ionic + osmotic), **PEG-6000** (pure osmotic),
and **Zn** (heavy metal) — measured on **Tomato** and **Cress**
seedlings, fits a four-parameter log-logistic curve per
(species × stressor) using **`drc::drm`**, extracts **ED50** (a.k.a.
IC50) with delta-method 95 % CIs, and compares species sensitivity
across stressors. The three-stressor design separates ionic vs purely
osmotic vs heavy-metal mechanisms.

## SS1 — Dose-response curves with inflection points

A flexible smoothing spline is fit through the replicate means on
log-dose, and zero crossings of its second derivative are flagged as
**inflection points**. The fitted **ED50** (from the LL.4 fit) is
overlaid as a blue dashed line; spline-derived inflection points are
black dashed.

```{r ss1-inflection, fig.height = 7}
library(ggplot2); library(dplyr)

inflect_points <- function(x, y, n_grid = 400) {
  ord <- order(x); x <- x[ord]; y <- y[ord]
  fit  <- smooth.spline(x, y, spar = 0.55)
  xs   <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = n_grid)
  d2   <- predict(fit, xs, deriv = 2)$y
  zc   <- which(diff(sign(d2)) != 0)
  # drop boundary artefacts near the edges of the sampled range
  margin <- 0.08 * (max(x) - min(x))
  xs_zc  <- xs[zc]
  xs_zc[xs_zc > min(x) + margin & xs_zc < max(x) - margin]
}

ss1 <- dat %>%
  group_by(species, stressor, dose) %>%
  summarise(mean_resp = mean(response), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(log_dose = log10(pmax(dose, 1)))

inflect_df <- ss1 %>%
  group_by(species, stressor) %>%
  summarise(infl = list(10 ^ inflect_points(log_dose, mean_resp)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::unnest(infl)

ed50_lines <- ed50 %>%
  transmute(species, stressor, ed50 = ED50)

# Prediction line on a fine grid extending down to x = 1 so the curve
# is visible across the full log-dose axis (not just the sampled doses).
ss1_pred <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(dat$stressor), function(st) {
  m  <- fits[[st]]
  xr <- range(dat$dose[dat$stressor == st & dat$dose > 0])
  xs <- exp(seq(log(1), log(xr[2]), length.out = 250))
  pr <- predict(m, newdata = expand.grid(dose = xs,
                                          species = levels(dat$species)))
  out <- expand.grid(dose = xs, species = levels(dat$species))
  out$mean_resp <- as.numeric(pr)
  out$stressor  <- st
  out
}))
ss1_pred$species  <- factor(ss1_pred$species,  levels = levels(dat$species))
ss1_pred$stressor <- factor(ss1_pred$stressor, levels = levels(dat$stressor))

ggplot(dat[dat$dose > 0, ], aes(dose, response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.3) +
  geom_line(data = ss1_pred, aes(dose, mean_resp),
            colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(data = inflect_df, aes(xintercept = infl),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(data = ed50_lines, aes(xintercept = ed50),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(species ~ stressor, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dose (log scale)",
       y = "Response (% of control)",
       title = "Dose-response curves with inflection points (SS1)",
       subtitle = "Blue = fitted ED50; grey = spline d2/dx2 zero crossings") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave("figures/ss1_inflection.png", width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

## SS2 — Trial-to-trial comparison

Three independent trials of the same experiment, overlaid per
(species × stressor). Points are trial means, error bars are ± SE
across replicates; the vertical green line marks the pooled ED50.

```{r ss2-trials, fig.height = 7}
ss2 <- dat %>%
  group_by(species, stressor, trial, dose) %>%
  summarise(mean_resp = mean(response),
            se_resp   = sd(response) / sqrt(n()),
            .groups   = "drop") %>%
  filter(dose > 0)

ggplot(ss2, aes(dose, mean_resp,
                colour   = trial,
                linetype = trial,
                shape    = trial)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_resp - se_resp,
                    ymax = mean_resp + se_resp),
                width = 0.05, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_vline(data = ed50_lines, aes(xintercept = ed50),
             colour = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(species ~ stressor, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`1` = "#1F78B4",
                                 `2` = "#1F78B4",
                                 `3` = "#E41A1C")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`1` = "dotted",
                                   `2` = "dashed",
                                   `3` = "solid")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`1` = 16, `2` = 17, `3` = 15)) +
  labs(x = "Dose (log scale)",
       y = "Response (% of control)",
       title = "Trial-to-trial comparison (SS2)",
       subtitle = "Mean +/- SE per trial; green line = pooled ED50",
       colour = "Trial", linetype = "Trial", shape = "Trial") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

ggsave("figures/ss2_trials.png", width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```


Lower ED50 = the species is *more* sensitive to that stressor.

## Sanity check vs ground truth

Because the data was simulated, we know the true ED50 used by the
generator. Compare the fitted ED50 to the truth:

```{r truth-check}
truth <- readRDS("data/truth.rds")
truth_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(truth), function(sp) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(truth[[sp]]), function(st) {
    data.frame(species = sp, stressor = st,
               true_ED50 = unname(truth[[sp]][[st]]["e"]))
  }))
}))
merged <- merge(ed50, truth_df, by = c("species", "stressor"))
merged$rel_error_pct <- 100 * (merged$ED50 - merged$true_ED50) / merged$true_ED50
knitr::kable(merged, digits = 2)
```

Relative errors are typically within a few percent — the kind of
agreement we'd want before trusting the fit on real data.

## Pairwise tests across species (per stressor)

```{r ed-test}
lapply(fits, EDcomp, percVec = c(50, 50), interval = "delta")
```

Confidence intervals on the ED50 *ratio* between species, per stressor.
A CI not crossing 1 means the two species differ significantly in
sensitivity.

## Disclaimer

Numbers are simulated from log-logistic curves with hand-chosen
parameters and Gaussian noise. The repo demonstrates the **drc-based
fitting workflow**, not a finding about real chemicals or species.
